text: The title page is written in calligraphy and printed from a block. Its lines are transcribed with the words divided as usual, since the calligraphy sets them close and lets them overlap; hamza and shadda are transcribed where they are written (الأرض, والأنهار, أبو, محمّد, الخوارزمىّ, الّذى, ألّفه, القلوذىّ, آدولف). The other vowel signs of the calligraphy (a ḍamma over the ب of كتاب and the ص of صورة, over the ه of استخرجه, ألّفه, بنسخه and تصحيحه, a fatḥa over the ع of طبع and the م of مدينة, a kasra under the alif of استخرجه and the س of سنة) and its small v-shaped signs over and under letters are not transcribed. The editor's name is written مژيك, with ژ, three dots over the ز, for the ž of Mžik, and Vienna ڤينا, with ڤ, three dots over the ف, for its v; موسى carries a short upright stroke over its final ى, and «ه» after the Hijri year 1345 and «م» after 1926 abbreviate the eras.

L10-L11: the two lines of the reprint are set in a heavy modern type, not in the calligraphy of the 1926 title page, which the reprint reproduces by offset (L01-L09, as frame 007): «أعيد طبعه سنة ١٩٦٢ / في أوفسيت مطبعة الرابطة ــ بغداد», reprinted in 1962 in offset at the Rābiṭa press, Baghdad. The type of these lines dots the final ي of في, where the calligraphy writes فى.
Blank, on the grey mottled paper of the reprint title page (frame 005).

The title page is written in calligraphy and printed from a block. Its lines are transcribed with the words divided as usual, since the calligraphy sets them close and lets them overlap; hamza and shadda are transcribed where they are written (الأرض, والأنهار, أبو, محمّد, الخوارزمىّ, الّذى, ألّفه, القلوذىّ, آدولف). The other vowel signs of the calligraphy (a ḍamma over the ب of كتاب and the ص of صورة, over the ه of استخرجه, ألّفه, بنسخه and تصحيحه, a fatḥa over the ع of طبع and the م of مدينة, a kasra under the alif of استخرجه and the س of سنة) and its small v-shaped signs over and under letters are not transcribed. The editor's name is written مژيك, with ژ, three dots over the ز, for the ž of Mžik, and Vienna ڤينا, with ڤ, three dots over the ف, for its v; موسى carries a short upright stroke over its final ى, and «ه» after the Hijri year 1345 and «م» after 1926 abbreviate the eras.
The 1962 reprint reproduces this page on its own title page (frame 005) and adds two lines in type.

L01: the basmala is written in calligraphy and printed from a block; hamza and shadda are transcribed where they are written, its other vowel signs are not, as on the title pages (frames 005 and 007). The folio of the Strasbourg manuscript, «(fol. 2ᵇ)», is printed in Latin type in the left margin beside it.

L02-L03: the head of the table, in a smaller type. Its columns, from the right: «(العدد)», the editor's running number in parentheses, and «[العدد كما تجده فى كتاب عجائب الأقاليم]», the number of the same entry in Suhrāb's ʿAjāʾib al-aqālīm in square brackets, both printed vertically, the second in two lines within square brackets; «اسماء المدن»; «الطول» and «العرض», each over two columns headed «درج» and «دقائق», degrees and minutes, printed vertically. On this page the column of the square brackets is empty. A rule stands above each pair of numeral cells of every entry, and above the cells of entries 1-6 also below them.
L04: the heading of the section, «اسماء المدن الّتى خلف خطّ الاستواء», stands between two small open stars, transcribed as asterisks.

The numerals of the table are written with letters, by their numerical values (abjad), the hundreds first: سه, 65; قنح, 158. The editor keeps the defective writing of the manuscript and corrects it only where dots stand in the wrong place or a number is impossible (introduction, frame 192, p. XXI). The loop of ف or ق printed without dots is transcribed ڡ (L06, L07, L10, L11, L12), and the final ب printed without its dot ٮ (L06, ڡكٮ); where the print dots the ق, it is transcribed ق (L08, قنح; L09, قسا). In the latitudes of L08 and L12 the print has ر; the editor states that in these numerals ر stands for 7 and not for 200 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed.

The sign for zero is a small circle with a stroke above it, the form which, the editor says, the Strasbourg manuscript alone uses for the zero (introduction, frame 192, p. XXI); it is written {z} in the page files and set as a small circle with a bar in the PDF.

L05: the longitude of entry 1, سه, and its minutes, the zero sign, are printed with a short line below them, under the س and the ه and under the circle of the zero sign; transcribed with the markup {u:…}. The pages of the introduction read so far do not say what the line marks.

L06: «اعا», as printed: an alif, an ع joined to a final alif, without the tooth or the dot of a ن (the join rises 4 px above the baseline); the editor's note b refers to the name «اعنا» at entry (1496).

L09: «قطيغوراا», as printed, with two alifs after the ر: the first stands 2 px from the ر, the second 14 px after the first; the editor's note e gives the name as «قطيغورا», with one alif, at entry (1726/1). The note mark f stands after the degrees of the longitude, قسا.

L10: a small irregular mark of ink, 7 px wide and 14 px high, stands above the left end of the longitude ڡسد; it is not shaped like the dots of the font, and a dot there would make an impossible number; it is not transcribed.

L12: the note mark i stands after the minutes of the latitude. In the footnotes the note i, the last line of the page, is printed without its mark; the editor's corrigenda (p. 163, frame 169) supply it.

The editor's notes refer to other entries of the book that name the same places: افاطا at (1142), written there «راقاطا»; اعا at (1496), «اعنا»; القمر at (1496); برقايا at (1498), «برقانا»; قطيغوراا at (1726/1); مودير at [105], an entry of Suhrāb; سوسه at (67) and (1726/1); and the minutes of the latitude of entry 8 at (1726/1).
Below the notes, at the left, the signature «1*» of the printed sheet; the page number «— ٣ —» stands at the foot, centred.

L01-L02: the two headings stand between small open stars, transcribed as asterisks. In L01 the latitude of the clime, «يو كر», is printed with a line above the two numerals, the line with which the edition marks numerals written with letters in the running text; transcribed with {ov:…}. The ر of كر stands for ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII): 16° 27'.
From this page the second column carries, in square brackets, the numbers of the same entries in Suhrāb's ʿAjāʾib al-aqālīm: [١]-[٣] at entries 9-11 and [٤] at entry 18; the other entries have none.

The angle brackets ⟨ ⟩: the editor's note a says that he marks between them what he supplies where the manuscript is damaged, has a gap or omits something, and with dots between them what he could not supply; the words of entry 9 are supplied from Suhrāb, whose book he cites as S. Transcribed as printed: ⟨مدينة ٮارس⟩ (L03), ⟨ٮد⟩ (L05, the degrees of the latitude), ⟨مدينة من⟩ (L08).

L03: «⟨مدينة ٮارس⟩ا», as printed: after the closing bracket and the note mark a stands a single alif, outside the brackets, the letter that the manuscript keeps of the damaged words; the first letter of ٮارس, a tooth joined to the alif, is printed without a dot.

Letters printed without their dots, transcribed so: the degrees of the longitude ٮٮ (L04) and of the latitude ٮٮ (L06), each a tooth joined to a final ب, both without dots, with two risers at the right end of the bowl, a tall and a short one, where the isolated ب has one (frame 013, L15); ڡكد (L07), the loop of ف or ق without dots; ٮد (L05) and ٮارس (L03), the tooth without its dot; ى, the final form without dots (L03, the degrees of the longitude, 10). The ق of قعٮ (L08) has its two dots, printed small; the print of this cell is blurred, and the shape between the ق and the final ٮ is that of a medial ع.

L09-L11: for the three ports of China, entries 15-17, the print sets a single zero sign in the middle of each pair of columns, under the rules of the longitude and of the latitude; transcribed as a zero sign spanning the two columns.
L05: the editor's note c says that the manuscript is damaged at دنقلة but the reading is certain; note d, that the degrees of the latitude are damaged and are supplied from S.
The page number «— ٤ —» stands at the foot, centred.

The table goes on from frame 010 without a heading: the cities of the first clime, entries 19-34. The folio of the Strasbourg manuscript, «(fol. 3ᵃ)», is printed in Latin type in the left margin beside entry 34 (L16).

L06: the latitude of Ṣanʿāʾ is printed «⟨ٮد ل⟩», the degrees and the minutes within one pair of angle brackets, the whole latitude supplied by the editor (note f); it is transcribed with the opening bracket in the degrees cell and the closing one in the minutes cell.
L03: the minutes of the latitude are printed «ي⟨ه⟩»: the ي stands outside the angle brackets, and only the ه is supplied (note c).

L04: above the final س of الفس stands a short stroke, 16 px long, slanting down to the left, in the shape and place of a fatḥa; transcribed as a fatḥa, «الفسَ». The editor's note mark d stands after it.

Letters printed without their dots, transcribed so: سماٮ (L01, the final letter); ڡٮاٮا (L15), the name of entry 30, قنانا (L12), printed without its dots, which the editor's note h identifies with entry 33; in the numerals ٮح (L01, the degrees of the longitude; L05, L10, the degrees of the latitude, where L01 prints يح with the two dots of the ي below the tooth), سٮ (L02), ٮد (L06) and عٮ (L14, L15), the tooth or the final ب without a dot; ٮ (L12, L15), the isolated ب without its dot, with one riser at the right end of the bowl; ٮٮ (L04, L08, L13, L16), a tooth joined to a final ب, both without dots, with two risers at the right end of the bowl, a tall and a short one, as يٮ and يب on frame 013 (L14, L11); ٮه (L08, the minutes of the longitude; L09, the degrees of the latitude), a tooth joined to a final ه, without its dot, the form printed with its dots in يه (L02-L04, L16). The longitude of entry 30 (L12), عب, has its dot.

The degrees of the latitude of entries 20 (ح), 29 (و), 30 and 33 (ٮ) and 32 (⟨د⟩) are printed with a single letter, a number below 10, where the latitude of the first clime is 16° 27' (frame 010, L01), entries 19 and 21 have يح and يه, entries 23 and 28 ٮح, entries 22, 26, 31 and 34 ٮٮ, and entry 27 ٮه, which read with a ي gives 15; the editor's notes do not comment on them. Transcribed as printed.
L08: the minutes of the latitude, ك, are printed with the small inner stroke of the letter, not with a line below.
The page number «— ٥ —» stands at the foot, centred.
L01: the bracket of the numbers of Suhrāb holds two numbers, «١٨» above «٥٨», printed one above the other within one pair of square brackets; transcribed «[١٨ ٥٨]».

L07-L11: entries 41-45, ʿAlwa Baḥriyya, Fazzān, Zaghāwa, Kawkaw and Ghāna, are printed without the word «مدينة» and without numbers of Suhrāb. A short horizontal stroke crosses the left parenthesis of the running number «(٤٥)» (L11), a flaw of the print.
L04-L06: «في» is printed with the two dots of the final ي in L04 and L05, «فى» without them in L06; transcribed as printed. L07: «بحريّة» and L08: «فزّان» are printed with a shadda.

Letters printed without their dots, transcribed so (the editor keeps the defective writing of the manuscript): in the names مسڡلى (L12; the loop of ف or ق, a round loop with a counter standing on the line, as the medial ف of the font, where the medial ع of صنعاء, frame 011, L06, is a solid, flat-topped form), مودٮرس (L13; at entry (1188) the name is written موزيرس, with ز and ي), فيرواٮ (L14, the final ب), ڡطرا (L15; at entry (1187) قطرا), اٮودى (L17, the tooth before the و) and مروٮا (L18, the tooth before the alif); in the numerals ڡ (L03, an isolated ف), ڡد, ڡر, ڡط (L04-L06), ڡٮ (L13), ڡٮه (L14, L15), ڡٮح (L17), the loop without dots, and سٮ (L08), ٮا (L08, L09), ٮو (L14, L18), the tooth or the final ب without its dot, ٮٮ (L04, L07), a tooth joined to a final ب, both without dots, with two risers at the right end of the bowl where the isolated ب has one, and ٮه (L02, the degrees of the latitude; L09, L13, L15-L17, the minutes of the longitude; L10, L18, the minutes of the latitude), a tooth joined to a final ه, without its dot. Where the print dots them they are transcribed with their dots: قى (L12), قير (L16), فك (L18), يه, يد, يج.

L14, L15, L17: between the loop and the final ه (L14, L15) or the ح (L17), a short tooth without a dot that rises above the joining stroke, with no part below it, where the medial م of these numerals is a diamond that stands out above and below the stroke (frame 013, L13, «ڡمح») or is set under the ق (frame 082, L16, «قمط»); transcribed ڡٮه and ڡٮح, which read with ق and ي give 115 and 118, beside قى, 110 (L12), and قير, 117 (L16).

L05: the longitude ڡر: the loop of ف or ق joined to a ر, in the place of a value between those of the other cities of al-Mīdh, ڡد ل and ڡط (L04, L06). In these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed. So also قير (L16).
L08-L09: the degrees of the latitude, ٮا: a tooth joined at its foot to an alif, without dots; transcribed so.
L18: the longitude فك, with the dot of the ف and the stroke of the ك printed, as printed.
The page number «— ٦ —» stands at the foot, centred.

The table goes on from frame 012 without a heading: the cities of the first clime, entries 53-68. Entries 56 and 58 have no numbers of Suhrāb; at entry 54 the square brackets hold two numbers, «٣٢» above «٥٧», transcribed «[٣٢ ٥٧]».

L01: «ڡل⟨م⟩ادى», as printed: the letter between the angle brackets is a medial م with its joining stroke, which the editor supplies where the manuscript has a gap (note a); the first letter, the loop of ف or ق, is printed without dots.

Letters printed without their dots, transcribed so: in the names ڡرسقورى (L07; a loop raised above the line and joined by a stroke on the line to the ر, the loop of ف or ق; an isolated و stands on the line and goes straight into its tail), ڡل⟨م⟩ادى (L01), ٮسر (L02; an initial tooth before the س), ماحوٮوں (L03, L04; the tooth before the second و, and the final ں, a bowl without its dot), حاٮرى (L05, the tooth before the ر), ٮاٮٮوقا (L09; three teeth: one before the first alif and two before the و) and طرٮعلوفن (L10, the tooth before the ع); in the numerals the loop of ف or ق without dots, ڡك (L01), ڡكا (L02-L04), ڡكه (L05, L07), ڡكح (L08), ڡمد (L10), ڡمو (L11, L12), ڡمح (L13), ڡسح (L15) and ڡعه (L16), and the tooth or the final ب without its dot, ٮا (L01), ٮو (L02, L03, L10), ٮح (L08), ٮه (L02, L03, L06, L07, L10, L13, the minutes of the longitude; L05, L11, L12, the minutes of the latitude; a tooth joined to a final ه, the form that L04 prints with the dot of the ن, نه), ٮٮ (L09; a tooth joined to a final ب, with two risers at the right end of the bowl, as يٮ in L14) and the final letters of يٮ and قنٮ (L14). With their dots: قكا (L06) and قل (L09), the ق with its two dots; قنٮ (L14), the ق with two dots and the ن with one; ز (L04), يو (L05), ير (L06), يه (L07, L10), يب (L11), ج (L12) and ب (L15). The isolated ه, 5 (L07, the degrees of the latitude), is a small round ring.

L01: a small dark speck, 5 px wide and 4 px high, stands below and 8 px to the left of the tooth of the latitude ٮا, where the dots of the font are 8 to 10 px across and stand under the tooth; it is not transcribed as a dot.
L15: the dot of the latitude ب is printed faintly, in grey, below the middle of the letter; transcribed ب.
L14: the three dots of the ث of قرداثر are printed as one mark; the final letter of the longitude قنٮ is a flat bowl without a dot below.
L16: the latitude of entry 68 is printed with the zero sign in the degrees and ك in the minutes, 0° 20'.
The page number «— ٧ —» stands at the foot, centred.

The table goes on from frame 013 without a heading: the last four cities of the first clime, entries 69-72; entry 72 has no number of Suhrāb. Then the heading of the second clime and of its cities, set between small open stars, as on frame 010; the folio of the Strasbourg manuscript, «(fol. 3ᵇ)», is printed in Latin type in the right margin beside the first heading (L05), where on frames 009 and 011 it stands in the left margin.

L05: the latitude of the second clime, «كد ō», 24° 0', is printed with a line above the numeral and the zero sign, as the latitude of the first clime on frame 010; transcribed with {ov:…}. In both headings the alif of الإقليم carries a hamza below, printed under the ligature لا; in the first it is small, 13 px wide. L06: «الّتى», with a shadda over the ل.
A small round dot, 13 px across, stands in the space between the two headings, below the end of عرضه; it belongs to neither line and is not transcribed.

L09: an asterisk stands after مدينة, «حرمى مدينة* الكبيرة», raised like the editor's note marks. With it the editor marks the forms against the grammar of the classical language that he keeps from the manuscript, among them an indefinite noun with a definite attribute (introduction, frame 184, p. XXIX), as مدينة الكبيرة here; transcribed as printed.

Letters printed without their dots, transcribed so: in the numerals the loop of ف or ق without dots, ڡعه, ڡعو, ڡعر (L01-L03); the tooth without its dots, ٮح (L07, L08, L11), ٮط (L09), ٮه (L02, the minutes of the longitude; L13, L15, the degrees of the longitude), a tooth joined to a final ه, and ٮو (L14, the degrees of the longitude), a tooth joined to a و; and the isolated ب without its dot, with one riser at the right end of its bowl, ٮ (L03). Where the print dots the numerals they are transcribed with their dots: يط (L10), يد (L12).
L12: the degrees of the longitude, يد: a small dot, 7 px across and lighter than the dots of the font, stands 13 px above the tooth of the ي, whose two dots stand below it; it is not transcribed.

L11, L14: the degrees of the latitude are printed «كٮ», a long oblique stroke over a flat bowl, 88 and 103 px wide, without the small inner stroke of the isolated ك: the ك joined to the final ب without its dot, 22. The isolated ك, 20, is about 35 to 38 px wide and has the small inner stroke (L08, the minutes of the latitude); the ك joined to the final ب with its dot, «كب», is 81 to 89 px wide (frame 085, L02; frame 089, L01). Frame 085 prints «كب ك», with the dot, 22° 20′, as the latitude of a point of the coast (L02), and the same group without the dot, «كٮ ك», for a later point between 24° 0′ (L05) and 21° 0′ (L08) (L06); the latitude of the third clime is «ل كٮ», 30° 22′ (frame 017, L13), as the first clime has 16° 27′ (frame 010, L01). Read so, the latitudes of Atfuwā and Suwān are 22° 45′ and 22° 30′. The isolated ه, 5 (L01, the degrees of the latitude), is a small round ring; «ٮه» (L02, L13, L15) is the tooth of a ن or a ي joined to a final ه, the form that frame 013 (L04) prints with the dot of the ن, نه.

L13-L15: the degrees of the longitudes of Bilāq, Suwān and al-Qaṣr are printed «ٮه», «ٮو» and «ٮه», a tooth without its dot joined to the next letter; read with a ن they give 55° 25', 56° 0' and 55° 50', beside the longitude of the next places on the Nile, Isnā and Armant, ٮو, 56 (frame 015, L01, L02).
The page number «— ٨ —» stands at the foot, centred.

The table goes on from frame 014 without a heading: the cities of the second clime, entries 82-97. Only entry 92 has the word «مدينة». Entries 82-86 and 88-94 have no numbers of Suhrāb. The number at entry 87, «[١٢٣]», stands outside the order of the numbers of the neighbouring entries, [٥٩]-[٦٧] on frame 014 and [٦٨]-[٧٠] at entries 95-97; transcribed as printed.

L08: the name of entry 89, «ڡصرى», is printed without dots on its first letter, the initial loop of ف or ق; transcribed so. The editor's notes do not comment on it. All other letters of the names on this page are printed with their dots.

L11: the degrees of the latitude are printed «ك⟨..⟩»: after the ك, two dots between angle brackets, the editor's sign for what he could not supply (frame 010, note a), then the note mark g. This ك has the small inner stroke of the letter.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: the tooth without its dot, ٮو (L01, L02), ٮر (L03, L04) and ٮح (L05, L14) in the degrees of the longitude, ٮر (L14, L15) and ٮح (L16) in the degrees of the latitude; the final ب without its dot in سٮ (L09, the degrees of the longitude); ں (L04, the minutes of the latitude), the bowl of a final ن without its dot. With their dots: نز (L12, L13), the ن with its dot above the tooth and the ز with its dot above the head of the letter, two dots side by side.

L03, L04, L14, L15: the degrees, ٮر, a tooth without its dot joined to a ر without a dot: in these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed. L12, L13 print the ز with its dot, نز.

L01, L07, L10: the degrees of the latitude are printed «كٮ», a long oblique stroke over a flat bowl, 88 to 92 px wide, without the small inner stroke of the isolated ك: the ك joined to the final ب without its dot, 22 (frame 014, L11); the isolated ك, 20, of L11 has the inner stroke. Read so, 22° 0′, 22° 35′ and 22° 0′. L02, L03: the minutes of the longitude, ه, 5, are printed as a small round ring, the isolated letter; transcribed ه. L09: the minutes of the latitude, «ٮه», are a tooth without its dot joined to a final ه; transcribed ٮه.
L12: «الزمرّد», with a shadda over the ر. L15: «سبأ», with a hamza over the alif.
In note d a dark round spot lies on the lower stroke of the ص of the manuscript reading الاڡصر, joined to it on the line, not below it where the dots of the font stand; it is not read as a dot.
The page number «— ٩ —» stands at the foot, centred.

The table goes on from frame 015 without a heading: the cities of the second clime, entries 98-114. Entry 109 has no number of Suhrāb. The folio of the Strasbourg manuscript, «(fol. 4ᵃ)», is printed in Latin type in the right margin beside entry 110 (L13), as on frame 014.

L11: the second word of the name is printed «امق»: an alif, then an initial م joined to a final ق with its two dots, without a tooth between them; transcribed as printed. A short horizontal stroke crosses the left parenthesis of the running number «(١٠٨)», a flaw of the print.

L14: an asterisk stands after واغلة, «اوموره واغلة* بين البحرين», raised like the editor's note marks: the editor's sign for a form against the grammar of the classical language that he keeps from the manuscript (introduction, frame 184, p. XXIX); transcribed as printed. The two dots of the ة of واغلة are printed as one mark touching the top of the letter.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: the tooth without its dots, ٮط (L03, L08, L13), ٮو (L06) and ٮح (L11) in the degrees of the latitude; the loop of ف or ق without dots, ڡد (L13, the degrees of the longitude); the final ب without its dot, صٮ (L15, the degrees of the longitude). With their dots: يز (L01), the ي with its two dots and the ز with its dot, 17.

L04, L17: the degrees of the longitude, سر and صر: in these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed. In L01 the latitude is printed with a dotted ز, يز.
L06: below the tooth of the degrees of the latitude, ٮو, stands a small dark speck, 5 px across, where the dots of the font are 10-11 px; it is not transcribed as a dot.

The degrees of the latitude of L09, L10, L12, L14 and L16 are printed «كٮ», a long oblique stroke over a flat bowl, 78 to 89 px wide, without the small inner stroke of the isolated ك: the ك joined to the final ب without its dot, 22 (frame 014, L11). The isolated ك, 20, of the minutes (L05, the minutes of the longitude and of the latitude; L09, the minutes of the latitude; L15, the minutes of the longitude) has the inner stroke. Read so, the latitudes are 22° 20′ (L09), 22° 30′ (L10, L12) and 22° 0′ (L14, L16).
L02: «جدّة», with a shadda over the د. L04: «مكّة», with a shadda over the ك. L05: «الطائف», with a hamza over the tooth before the ف.

L08: a small dot stands below the ٨ of the number of Suhrāb, «[٧٨]», a speck of the print; it is not transcribed. L17: in «البحر» the ل is printed apart from the following ب, and a small speck stands below the alif.
The page number «— ١٠ —» stands at the foot, centred.

L01-L04 end the outer western and northern sea: after the point of latitude 72 (L01) the coast passes to the latitude «عح», returns from there to the longitude of one degree, «ويرجع من هناك الى طول جزء واحد» (L02), and returns along the longitude «ا {z}», 1° 0′, from the latitude «عح» to the latitude «{z} ى», 0° 10′, on the meridian of one degree, «على سمت طول جزء واحد», and so back to the place with whose mention it began, «فيرجع الى الموضع الّذى فيه ابتدأنا بذكره» (L03-L04): the first point of p. 66 (frame 072, L03), longitude 1° 0′ and latitude 0° 10′ (note a). L04 ends with a small open star, transcribed as an asterisk. «جزء» has a hamza on the line; «الّذى» a shadda over the ل; «ابتدأنا» a hamza over the alif.

L05-L07: the heading of the next section, in the large type, between two small open stars, transcribed as asterisks: «* بحر طنجة وبحر مرطاسه وبحر أفريقيّة وبحر برقة وبحر مصر والشام وبحر ٮرقه ولزقه كلّها متّصلة بعضها ببعض *», the sea of Tangier, the sea of مرطاسه, the sea of Ifrīqiya, the sea of Barqa, the sea of Egypt and Syria, and the sea of ٮرقه and لزقه, all of them joined to one another. «أفريقيّة», with a hamza over the alif and a shadda over the ي; «كلّها», with a shadda over the ل; «متّصلة», with a shadda over the ت; «ببعض» is printed with a long kashida, the stretched joining stroke, before the ض, which is not transcribed. «مرطاسه» and «لزقه» end in ه, «برقة» in ة; «ٮرقه» begins with a tooth without a dot, joined to the ر.
